clue.text: Realizing endless oil could make chap stupendously wealthy

indicators.note: could make suggests the letters can be reworked into a new arrangement
endless means the word Realizing loses its final letter before use

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who strikes oil might become fabulously rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims Realizing to REALIZIN; with OIL those eleven letters are rearranged, signalled by 'could make'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanciful word for a person with countless millions, someone stupendously wealthy.

clue.text: Vitality's answer for one making kill

indicators.note: for means one letter stands in place of another in the word

parts.note: zip is vigour or vitality
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A lively response is what brings about a killing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' says A (answer) takes the place of I (one) in ZIP.
explanation.definitionFit: To zap someone is slang for killing them, especially with a ray gun.

clue.text: Artist using brass for ears

indicators.note: for ears means the word is heard rather than read, so its sound counts

parts.note: brass is cheek or insolence, so brassy talk is lippy

explanation.surface: A painter who works with brass musical instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: Brass here is British slang for cheek; LIPPY (cheeky) said aloud matches the painter's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Filippo Lippi and his son Filippino were Florentine Renaissance painters.

clue.text: Fashionable paper folded before finishing year's investigation

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: before finishing means the word stops short of its last letter

parts.note: a quire is a set of folded sheets of paper
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A trendy newspaper is creased before the year ends, prompting an inquest.
explanation.walkthrough: A quire is a traditional measure of paper, twenty-four sheets folded together; 'before finishing' clips its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An inquiry is a formal investigation into something.

clue.text: Some thread is necessary for binding foreign article

indicators.note: for binding means the first word wraps round the second

parts.note: needful means necessary
le is the French definite article

explanation.surface: Thread is needed to bind a foreign item.
explanation.definitionFit: A needleful is the length of thread put through a needle at one time, some thread.

clue.text: In Association missing Liberal is given black mark perhaps

indicators.note: missing means a letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: linked means in association

explanation.surface: Without the Liberal party, the alliance gets a black mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' removes L (Liberal) from LINKED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inked has been marked with ink, such as a black mark.

clue.text: Set off to walk slowly into river

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
to plod is to walk slowly

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to trudge into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England; 'Set off' is a verb phrase, as of a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: To explode a bomb is to set it off.

clue.text: Nothing odd in owning a rug

indicators.note: nothing odd means the odd-placed letters are discarded, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: Owning a rug has nothing strange about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rug is slang for a wig or toupee.

clue.text: Identical paths, one taking short route left, perversely

parts.note: two paths that are the same, each a way

indicators.note: one taking means the second way takes another piece inside it

parts.note: the second of the two identical ways
RD is the short form of road, a route

explanation.surface: Two matching paths, one with a shortcut on the left, laid out oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Identical paths' supplies the same word twice; 'one taking' says only the second of them swallows the road abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Waywardly means in a self-willed, contrary manner, perversely.

clue.text: Compromises vegan diet, mistakenly eating a small piece of kidney

indicators.note: eating means one piece swallows the other
mistakenly suggests the letters are put together wrongly, a rearrangement
a small piece of a word here is just its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone compromises their vegan diet by eating a little kidney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistakenly' rearranges VEGAN DIET to GIVEANDTE, which, signalled by 'eating', takes in A plus K, the first letter of kidney.
explanation.definitionFit: Give-and-take, as a noun, is mutual concession, and its plural sense matches compromises.

clue.text: Nobody makes escape after defeat

indicators.note: after means this piece comes second

parts.note: to pip is to defeat narrowly
a squeak is a narrow escape

explanation.surface: Someone escapes after losing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nobody' reads as no person, but it is the noun: an unimportant person.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipsqueak is an insignificant person, a nobody.

clue.text: Is it broadcast as billed?

parts.note: reads as a doubt about schedule listings, but means television you are billed for to watch

explanation.surface: Is the programme shown as advertised?
explanation.definitionFit: Subscription television is broadcasting that viewers are billed for.

clue.text: Slight rolling of r's not finished with by way of introduction

indicators.note: introduction means a piece is introduced into another
not finished means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a trill is the rolled pronunciation of r
via means by way of

explanation.surface: A minor matter of rolling one's r's that is left incomplete.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivial and slight are synonyms meaning of little importance.

clue.text: Idiot rushing around making cry

indicators.note: around means the first word goes round the second

parts.note: tearing means rushing
a jerk is an idiot

explanation.surface: A fool dashing about reduces someone to tears.
explanation.definitionFit: A tear-jerking film is one designed to make the audience cry.

clue.text: Scenic picture from satellite brought into play

indicators.note: brought into means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a drama is a play
Io is a moon of Jupiter

explanation.surface: A view from space is worked into a stage production.
explanation.definitionFit: A diorama is a three-dimensional scene or scenic model.

clue.text: Church affirmative about decline, on reflection

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the second

parts.note: ay is an affirmative, yes

indicators.note: on reflection means the word is mirrored, read backwards

parts.note: to ebb is to decline

explanation.surface: The church says yes to its decline, after some thought.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbey is a monastic church.

clue.text: Metal handle for girl one put in chimney

parts.note: Beryl is a girl's name, a handle

indicators.note: put in means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: lum is a Scottish word for chimney
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A girl's name, with one placed in a chimney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' sets I inside LUM, a Scottish word for chimney.
explanation.definitionFit: Beryllium is a light metallic chemical element.

clue.text: Slow in terrible heat, coming in weakened

indicators.note: coming in means a piece is placed inside another

parts.note: faded means weakened

indicators.note: terrible suggests the letters are in a dreadful jumble

explanation.surface: Someone becomes sluggish in awful heat and wilts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slow' here means dim-witted, not unhurried.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatheaded means stupid, slow on the uptake.

clue.text: A test for vehicle climbing up to old Mexican plant

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for UK vehicles
till means up to

explanation.surface: A vehicle test for climbing as far as an old Mexican shrub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns A plus MOT upwards to TOMA. The MOT is Britain's yearly roadworthiness test for vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: The tomatillo is a Mexican plant bearing small green fruit.

clue.text: City's retrograde step, surrounding line judge initially

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the word
retrograde means moving backwards, so the word is reversed
surrounding means the first word goes round the second

parts.note: a measure is a step taken

explanation.surface: A city takes a backward step, with a line judge involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' puts L inside MEASURE; 'retrograde' turns MELASURE to ERUSALEM, after J from 'judge initially'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerusalem is the ancient holy city in the Middle East.

clue.text: Lesbian seems confused about a kiss

indicators.note: about means the anagram goes round the other piece
confused suggests the letters are jumbled

parts.note: X is a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A gay woman seems bewildered by a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges SEEMS to SMESE, and 'about' puts it round A, giving SAMESE, then X.
explanation.definitionFit: Same-sex describes relationships between people of one gender, as a lesbian one is.

clue.text: Parts of the kingdom need some prophylactics

indicators.note: some means only part of the word is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: Parts of the realm require contraceptives.
explanation.walkthrough: The kingdom is the biological animal or plant kingdom, not a country.
explanation.definitionFit: In taxonomy, phyla are the major divisions of a biological kingdom.

parts.note: to roll is to flatten
to mop is to clean

explanation.definitionFit: A rollmop is a rolled pickled herring fillet served ready to eat.

clue.text: Cape in essence a waterproof coat

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: pith is the essence of something

clue.text: Touching rendition of Cat in the Hat?

parts.note: tile is slang for a hat

indicators.note: a rendition is a version, so the letters appear in a new order

explanation.surface: A moving performance of the children's book The Cat in the Hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Tile is old British slang for a hat; the surface borrows the title of a well-known children's book.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactile means relating to touch, so touching in the literal sense.

clue.text: Fine introduced in club for chopping tree

indicators.note: introduced in means one piece goes inside another
for chopping means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: an iron is a golf club
OK means fine

explanation.surface: A penalty imposed in a club for cutting down a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like a penalty, but it is the adjective, meaning all right.
explanation.definitionFit: The iroko is a large West African hardwood tree.

clue.text: Climbers struggle in extremes of iciness

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside another
extremes of means the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: to vie is to struggle or compete

explanation.surface: Mountaineers battle against the icy conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbers' suggests mountaineers, but they are plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivies are climbing plants.

clue.text: Novice brought in by Middlesbrough banker to manage contract

indicators.note: brought in by means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Tees is the river at Middlesbrough, a banker being something with banks
L is a learner, a novice
to cope is to manage

explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' is a river, something with banks; Middlesbrough is a town in north-east England on the Tees. 'brought in by' puts L inside TEES.
explanation.definitionFit: To telescope is to shorten or contract by sliding sections together.

clue.text: 4 may pass through this study

to study is to look at closely

explanation.definitionFit: A needle's eye takes thread, and to eye something is to study it.

clue.text: Leg in contest European lost

indicators.note: lost means a letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: a game is a contest

explanation.surface: A leg injury suffered in a match the Europeans lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes E from GAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Gam is slang for a leg, especially a shapely one.

clue.text: There's more than one to a cell in convent

definitions.text: There's more than one to a cell in convent

parts.words: There's more than one to a cell in convent
parts.note: pictures a nun's cell, but means a biological cell in a female, which carries a pair of the sex-determining kind
